status.en: 110 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 18% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 110 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 18 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Gunmen attacked a village in Plateau State, killing 17 people, while armed men killed 13 Niger soldiers in Sanam and bandits abducted nine residents in Zamfara. The Plateau governor condemned the killings and ordered stronger security, and the Niger State governor directed protection for residents after the Zamfara abductions. In addition, gunmen injured four people in an overnight attack on a Plateau community and killed 16 there, and a separate incident injured one supporter at a political gathering in Edo. The conflict remains intense, with 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn angrep en landsby i Plateau State, og drepte 17 personer, mens bevæpnede menn drepte 13 soldater fra Niger i Sanam og banditter bortførte ni innbyggere i Zamfara. Guvernøren i Plateau fordømte drapene og beordret strengere sikkerhet, og guvernøren i Niger State ga beskytte innbyggerne etter bortføringene i Zamfara. I tillegg såret våpenbærende menn fire personer i et overnattingsangrep på et samfunn i Plateau og drepte 16 der, og en separat hendelse såret en tilhenger på en politisk samling i Edo. Konflikten forblir intens, med 1 486 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
